clue.text: A month after one's torn from vehicle, wing found

indicators.note: after places the month at the end, following the shortened vehicle
something torn from a word is ripped out of it, so the letter for one leaves the vehicle

parts.note: a train is a vehicle on rails
one is I, the Roman numeral
Sept is the short form of September, a month

explanation.surface: Someone tears a month off a calendar on a vehicle and finds a wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wing' sounds like a bird's or plane's, but here it is part of a church building; 'torn from' and 'after' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, the wing crossing the nave.

clue.text: Appear to find vessel in sheep

indicators.note: in puts the vessel inside the sheep's letters

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep
an urn is a vessel for ashes or tea

explanation.surface: An odd instruction to go looking for a pot inside a flock.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is the phrasal verb for arriving or appearing, as a guest does at a party.

clue.text: Evaluate a drug in seconds

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in sets the drug among the seconds

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second; plural seconds gives several, here four S
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Testing a pill within moments, as in a quick lab check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts E inside SSSS (two pairs of S for seconds), after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess something is to judge its value or quality, a direct synonym of evaluate.

clue.text: Eight runs requiring overthrow, of course

indicators.note: an overthrow upsets the existing order, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Cricket: eight runs scored from an overthrow, which naturally happens.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an overthrow is a wild return that lets batsmen run extra; here it signals an anagram of EIGHT RUNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sure thing is an informal phrase of agreement meaning certainly, just as of course is.

clue.text: Sovereign's body in the throne room?

definitions.text: Sovereign's body in the throne room?

parts.words: Sovereign's body in the throne room?
parts.note: a privy is an old word for a toilet, jokingly a throne room

explanation.surface: Picturing the monarch's advisers gathered beside the royal throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The Privy Council is the formal body of advisers to the British monarch; 'throne' is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: The Privy Council is the advisory body that serves the British sovereign.

clue.text: In which miscreant is locked, showing bloomers

definitions.meaning: the old punishment frame clamping an offender's ankles in the village square
a flowering garden plant, also called gillyflower

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer is locked up and his underwear is on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like underwear, but means plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks were a wooden punishment device, and stocks are also fragrant garden flowers.

clue.text: Powerful eastern dynasty adopting western accent

indicators.note: adopting takes something in, so the dynasty's letters enclose the western letter

parts.note: the Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907

explanation.surface: A mighty Chinese dynasty picks up a Western way of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a nasal or distinctive regional accent in speech.

clue.text: Premier of clothing outlets ordered garment for women

indicators.note: the premier is the first, so this takes the opening letter of clothing
ordered means put into a new order, so the letters of outlets are rearranged

explanation.surface: The top clothing shops order in a new women's garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier of' gives C; 'ordered' rearranges OUTLETS into ULOTTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Culottes are women's knee-length trousers cut to look like a skirt.

clue.text: Individual copies upped the price

indicators.note: upped means raised, and in a down entry raising a word reads it bottom to top

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them, so copies gives apes
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Individual items whose duplicates pushed the price up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upped' reads upwards because this is a down entry; 'Individual' is an adjective, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Separate as an adjective means distinct or individual, existing apart from others.

clue.text: Hold back to stop fall

parts.note: a rest is a stop or pause
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Advice to grab something to break a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or keep under control.

clue.text: Beer, or punch

definitions.meaning: a slang word for beer or ale
a heavy blow with the fist

explanation.definitionFit: Wallop is British slang for beer, and also means a hard punch.

clue.text: Drunken soak with brunette, old movie star

indicators.note: a drunken person staggers about, so the letters of these words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A drunk is seen with a dark-haired woman, both old film stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges SOAK and BRUNETTE into the actor's name; 'soak' looks like a drunkard.
explanation.definitionFit: Buster Keaton was a silent-film comedian, a star of early cinema.

clue.text: Winning some games, get emotional

parts.note: being up means ahead in a contest
a set is a group of games in tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player ahead in the match becomes tearful.
explanation.definitionFit: Upset as an adjective describes someone distressed or emotionally troubled.

clue.text: Child got nurse off her trolley by day's end

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter
off one's trolley means crazy, so the letters of these words go wild

explanation.surface: A child gets a nurse to go mad by the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'day's end' gives Y; 'off her trolley' rearranges GOT NURSE into OUNGSTER. Off one's trolley is British slang for crazy, and the trolley suggests a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A youngster is a young person, a child.

clue.text: What a volleyball team selector might choose as punishment?

definitions.text: What a volleyball team selector might choose as punishment?

parts.words: What a volleyball team selector might choose as punishment?
parts.note: a volleyball side has six players, so the selector picks the top half-dozen; the phrase is also an old caning penalty

explanation.surface: A coach picks the best players, but the result is a punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: Six of the best was a beating of six strokes of the cane, once used in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names six strokes of the cane, a traditional school punishment.

clue.text: Fancy talk in support of English party

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece supporting another sits beneath it

parts.note: Lab is short for the Labour Party
to orate is to talk formally

explanation.surface: A speech made backing the English Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a major UK political party. 'in support of' puts ORATE beneath E and LAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective means ornate or fancy, full of detail.

clue.text: Wood put up by man in black at a place of execution

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means raised, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood
a goth dresses in black clothing
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gallows of wood erected by a black-clad hangman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns LOG into GOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Golgotha is the hill where Jesus was crucified, a place of execution.

clue.text: It blows in the wind, awful cold?

definitions.meaning: a long ribbon or pennant that flutters in a breeze
a heavy cold with a running nose

explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a ribbon that flutters in the wind, and a streaming cold is a bad one.

clue.text: Old man passing round some marijuana, I ran, 'e got collared!

indicators.note: passing something round turns it about, so these letters are read backwards
some of the text gives a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A man flees after sharing a joint and his friend gets arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run from 'marijuana, I ran, 'e got collared', and 'passing round' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An octogenarian is someone in their eighties, an elderly person.

clue.text: Child reared on rubbish, order shoved down one's throat?

indicators.note: reared means raised up, so the word reads upwards in this down entry

parts.note: a kid is a child
tat is British slang for cheap rubbish

explanation.surface: A child raised on junk is forced to swallow orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reared' reads upwards in this down entry; 'on' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed without consultation, forced on people.

clue.text: Guide rounding pole with an African

indicators.note: rounding means going round, so the guide surrounds the pole

parts.note: a key is a guide that explains symbols on a map
N is the north pole
taken as written

explanation.surface: A guide circling the pole with a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounding' puts N inside KEY to make KENY.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenyan describes a person from Kenya, an East African country.

clue.text: Head parting company with meandering, loose syrup

indicators.note: loose means free and disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the head of a word is its first letter, which leaves the word

explanation.surface: A loose stream of syrup winding about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head parting company with' removes M from MEANDERING; 'loose' rearranges EANDERING.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadine is a sweet red syrup made from pomegranates.

clue.text: Bill given award, a brick

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a bill
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Bill receives an honour for being a solid friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a brick' is British slang for a reliable person, the surface's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is a sun-dried brick of clay and straw.

clue.text: Tomato ultimately has to be a fruit

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter is taken

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: A tomato is, after all, a fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes O from Tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: An olive is the small oily fruit of the olive tree.

clue.text: Instrument for Siamese twins, perhaps?

indicators.note: twins means two alike, so the cat appears twice

parts.note: a Siamese is a cat, and a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An instrument for conjoined twins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siamese twins' suggests conjoined people, but Siamese is a breed of cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom-tom is a drum beaten with the hands, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Bird first to tell, breaking modest secret

indicators.note: breaking means getting into, so the pieces go inside the modest word

parts.note: shy means modest, retiring
a teal is a small duck

indicators.note: first to means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A bird breaks a shy creature's secret by telling it first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' is the container signal, and 'secret' is the definition read as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealthy means done secretly or quietly, so as to avoid notice.

clue.text: Old squeezes about? Yes!

indicators.note: squeezes means squeezes in, so the old word holds the other

parts.note: aged means old
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: An old person squeezes a hand and answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeezes' signals a container; the exclamation 'Yes!' is the definition, said as a word of assent.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed is an exclamation of assent, like saying yes.

clue.text: Not taken down, leader in battle held — to be so?

definitions.text: Not taken down, leader in battle held — to be so?

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the other word encloses the letter

parts.note: food not taken down is not swallowed

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A commander who held out was not defeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held' puts B (leader in battle) inside UNEATEN; the clue as a whole is a definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbeaten means undefeated, which a commander who held would be.
